# TEST — development with live file editing.
#
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.test.yml up
#   open http://localhost:5173
#
# Differences from deploy: sources are mounted from the host, the frontend runs
# in Vite dev mode with HMR on :5173 and proxies /api, the server runs with
# --reload, and two "device" containers with sshd and a demo service let the
# terminal, files and tunnels be tested without hardware.
#
# The devices need an enrollment token from the panel ("Enroll"), so they sit
# behind a profile — see device-a below.

services:
  app:
    # The prebuilt panel image: dependencies are already in it, sources are
    # mounted on top and --reload watches them. Build it beforehand:
    #   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.build.yml build panel
    image: sazonovanton/radm:${RADM_VERSION:-latest}
    working_dir: /app
    command:
      - uvicorn
      - radm.main:app
      - --host=0.0.0.0
      - --port=8000
      - --reload
      - --reload-dir=/app/server/radm
      - --reload-dir=/app/shared
    environment:
      RADM_SECRET_KEY: dev-only-secret-not-for-production
      # install.sh hands agents exactly this address, so it must be
      # reachable from inside the compose network.
      RADM_PUBLIC_URL: http://app:8000
      RADM_BASE_DOMAIN: localhost
      RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN: tunnel.localhost
      RADM_ADMIN_USER: ${RADM_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      RADM_ADMIN_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]}
      # uvicorn listens directly, with no proxy in front: X-Forwarded-For
      # must not be trusted at all.
      RADM_TRUSTED_PROXIES: "0"
      # The SPA lives on Vite (:5173) and proxies /api here, so the websocket
      # Origin is its address, not RADM_PUBLIC_URL.
      RADM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "http://localhost:${RADM_TEST_WEB_PORT:-5173},http://127.0.0.1:${RADM_TEST_WEB_PORT:-5173}"
      RADM_METRICS_INTERVAL: "5"
      RADM_LOG_LEVEL: ${RADM_LOG_LEVEL:-INFO}
      RADM_DATA_DIR: /data
      RADM_DATABASE_URL: sqlite+aiosqlite:////data/radm.db
      PYTHONUNBUFFERED: "1"
      HTTP_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
      HTTPS_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
      NO_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_NOPROXY:-localhost,127.0.0.1,app,web,device-a,device-b}
    # Lets RADM_BUILD_PROXY point at a relay on the host
    # (http://host.docker.internal:3128).
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    volumes:
      - ../server:/app/server
      - ../shared:/app/shared
      # The install scripts live in agent/install and arrive with this mount.
      - ../agent:/app/agent
      - radm-test-data:/data
    ports:
      # Configurable, because 8000 is almost always taken on a work machine.
      - "127.0.0.1:${RADM_TEST_API_PORT:-8000}:8000"
    networks: [radm]

  web:
    # node:20, not alpine: node_modules is mounted from the host, and the
    # esbuild and rollup binaries there are built against glibc — they will not
    # run in a musl image.
    image: node:20
    working_dir: /web
    command:
      - bash
      - -c
      - '[ -x node_modules/.bin/vite ] || npm install --no-audit --no-fund; exec npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0'
    environment:
      # Vite proxies /api here (see vite.config.ts), so cookies and websockets
      # behave exactly as they do in production.
      RADM_DEV_API: http://app:8000
      npm_config_proxy: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
      npm_config_https_proxy: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    volumes:
      # Mounted whole, node_modules included: the container installs nothing
      # if the host already has them, otherwise it does so on first start.
      - ../web:/web
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${RADM_TEST_WEB_PORT:-5173}:5173"
    depends_on: [app]
    networks: [radm]

  # The "device" containers, behind a profile because of the token:
  #   ENROLL_TOKEN=... docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.test.yml --profile devices up -d device-a
  device-a:
    # Only `image`, same as device-b: with `build` here one of the two
    # identical containers would build in place while the other failed on a
    # missing image. deploy/docker-compose.build.yml builds it.
    image: radm-test-device:latest
    hostname: pi-kitchen
    environment:
      PANEL_URL: http://app:8000
      ENROLL_TOKEN: [REDACTED]}
    depends_on: [app]
    networks: [radm]
    profiles: ["devices"]

  device-b:
    image: radm-test-device:latest
    hostname: pi-garage
    environment:
      PANEL_URL: http://app:8000
      ENROLL_TOKEN: [REDACTED]}
    depends_on: [app, device-a]
    networks: [radm]
    profiles: ["devices"]

volumes:
  radm-test-data:

networks:
  radm:

# A stand-in for a Raspberry Pi: sshd, python3, the agent, and a small web
# service to point a tunnel at. Lets the whole system be exercised end to end
# without hardware.
FROM debian:bookworm-slim

ARG HTTP_PROXY=""
ARG HTTPS_PROXY=""

# The proxy is scoped to this RUN and never becomes part of the image
# environment. Persisting it would leak into the agent at runtime, and the
# agent honours proxy variables — it would then try to reach the panel through
# a proxy that only ever existed on the build machine.
RUN HTTP_PROXY=$HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY=$HTTPS_PROXY \
    apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        openssh-server python3 curl ca-certificates procps \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# A normal login user, matching how a real board is set up.
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash pi && passwd -d pi \
    && mkdir -p /run/sshd /var/lib/radm

COPY deploy/test-device/entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh

ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]

"""One-time token guarding first-run setup.

``POST /api/auth/setup`` creates the first administrator, and whoever calls it
owns the panel and therefore every device in the fleet. Gating it on "no admin
exists yet" alone means the panel is up for grabs between ``docker compose up``
and the moment the operator reaches the browser — a window on a public domain
that a scanner can win.

So the panel issues a token at startup instead, prints it to the log and writes
it next to the database, and requires it in the setup call. Restarting the panel
rotates it; completing setup clears it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os

from radm.security.crypto import new_token, tokens_equal

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

TOKEN_FILE = "setup-token"

_token: str | None = None


def issue(data_dir: str) -> str:
    """Create the setup token, announce it, and return it."""
    global _token
    _token = [REDACTED]

    path = os.path.join(data_dir, TOKEN_FILE)
    try:
        # Written with 0600 from the start rather than chmod'ed afterwards, so
        # the token is never briefly readable by anyone else.
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as handle:
            handle.write(_token + "\n")
    except OSError as exc:
        log.warning("could not write %s: %s", path, exc)

    log.warning(
        "no administrator exists yet. Finish setup with this one-time token:\n"
        "    %s\n"
        "It is also in %s and is replaced every time the panel restarts.",
        _token,
        path,
    )
    return _token


def verify(candidate: str | None) -> bool:
    if not _token or not candidate:
        return False
    return tokens_equal(candidate, _token)


def clear(data_dir: str) -> None:
    """Retire the token once an administrator exists."""
    global _token
    _token = None
    try:
        os.unlink(os.path.join(data_dir, TOKEN_FILE))
    except OSError:
        pass


def pending() -> bool:
    return _token is not None

# BUILD — builds the images and starts nothing.
#
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.build.yml build
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.build.yml push   # if you use a registry
#
# `up` here would start the images bare, without environment, ports or volumes:
# docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.test.yml are what you run. The images
# hold everything needed to operate — the frontend (Vite → static files), the
# agent (radm-agent.pyz, identical on every architecture) and the server — so
# deploy needs no sources on the host.
#
# Behind a proxy: RADM_BUILD_PROXY in deploy/.env, and if it wants
# authentication, deploy/proxy-relay.py on the host (npm does not send
# credentials). See the comment in .env.example.

services:
  panel:
    image: sazonovanton/radm:${RADM_VERSION:-latest}
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile
      network: ${RADM_BUILD_NETWORK:-default}
      args:
        HTTP_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
        HTTPS_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
        NO_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_NOPROXY:-localhost,127.0.0.1}

  test-device:
    image: radm-test-device:latest
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/test-device/Dockerfile
      network: ${RADM_BUILD_NETWORK:-default}
      args:
        HTTP_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
        HTTPS_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_PROXY:-}
        NO_PROXY: ${RADM_BUILD_NOPROXY:-localhost,127.0.0.1}

# DEPLOY — the panel, with a Traefik in front of it or into one you already run.
#
#   cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env           # fill it in
#   cp deploy/.env.dns.example deploy/.env.dns   # DNS-01 credentials
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d
#
# COMPOSE_PROFILES in deploy/.env picks the mode: proxy — the Traefik below
# comes up and takes :80/:443; unset — the panel alone, on your proxy's network
# (RADM_TRAEFIK_* in .env). Routes are labels on the panel container, so the
# proxy has no config file of its own; nothing but the two .env comes from the
# host.

services:
  app:
    image: sazonovanton/radm:${RADM_VERSION:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      RADM_SECRET_KEY: ${RADM_SECRET_KEY:?set RADM_SECRET_KEY in deploy/.env}
      RADM_PUBLIC_URL: https://${RADM_BASE_DOMAIN}
      RADM_BASE_DOMAIN: ${RADM_BASE_DOMAIN}
      RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN: ${RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN}
      # The tunnel labels below are written for subdomain; switching to path
      # without rewriting them leaves the tunnels unreachable.
      RADM_TUNNEL_ROUTING: ${RADM_TUNNEL_ROUTING:-subdomain}
      RADM_ADMIN_USER: ${RADM_ADMIN_USER:-admin}
      RADM_ADMIN_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]}
      # Proxies in front of the panel. The client address is counted back from
      # the end of X-Forwarded-For, and only for connections coming from
      # RADM_TRUSTED_PROXY_NETWORKS.
      RADM_TRUSTED_PROXIES: ${RADM_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-1}
      RADM_METRICS_INTERVAL: ${RADM_METRICS_INTERVAL:-10}
      RADM_LOG_LEVEL: ${RADM_LOG_LEVEL:-INFO}
    volumes:
      - radm-data:/data
    expose:
      - "8000"
    networks: [proxy]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      start_period: 15s
    # Entrypoint and resolver default to the ones the Traefik below defines;
    # for a proxy of your own set both in .env.
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      # Which network the proxy reaches the panel over — matters when yours
      # has several.
      - "traefik.docker.network=${RADM_TRAEFIK_NETWORK:-radm}"
      - "traefik.http.services.radm.loadbalancer.server.port=8000"

      # --- panel ----------------------------------------------------------
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-panel.rule=Host(`${RADM_BASE_DOMAIN}`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-panel.entrypoints=${RADM_TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT:-websecure}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-panel.service=radm"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-panel.tls.certresolver=${RADM_TRAEFIK_CERTRESOLVER:-dns}"

      # --- device tunnels --------------------------------------------------
      # Host() has no wildcards, hence HostRegexp. Its unescaped dots match any
      # character — harmless: the panel checks the Host itself and 404s a stray
      # one (radm.tunnels.http_proxy.is_tunnel_host).
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.rule=HostRegexp(`^[a-z0-9-]+\\.${RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN}$$`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.entrypoints=${RADM_TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT:-websecure}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.service=radm"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.tls.certresolver=${RADM_TRAEFIK_CERTRESOLVER:-dns}"
      # Priority defaults to the length of the rule, so this long regexp would
      # outrank a neighbour's short Host() and swallow its traffic.
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.priority=1"
      # Traefik cannot derive an ACME name from a HostRegexp, so the wildcard
      # is asked for explicitly; the resolver must do DNS-01.
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.tls.domains[0].main=${RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN}"
      - "traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.tls.domains[0].sans=*.${RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN}"

      # For RADM_TUNNEL_ROUTING=path, replace the rule, the priority and both
      # domains[0] lines with one — HTTP-01 is then enough and .env.dns is not
      # needed:
      #   traefik.http.routers.radm-tunnels.rule=Host(`${RADM_TUNNEL_DOMAIN}`)

  traefik:
    profiles: [proxy]
    image: traefik:v3.3
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - "--providers.docker=true"
      # Only containers carrying traefik.enable=true are routed.
      - "--providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false"
      - "--entrypoints.web.address=:80"
      - "--entrypoints.websecure.address=:443"
      # The session cookie only gets the Secure flag on an https request, so
      # over plain HTTP the panel would work — and hand the session token to
      # anyone on the wire. Hence the redirect rather than an open :80.
      - "--entrypoints.web.http.redirections.entrypoint.to=websecure"
      - "--entrypoints.web.http.redirections.entrypoint.scheme=https"
      # DNS-01, because nothing else issues a wildcard. With
      # RADM_TUNNEL_ROUTING=path swap the challenge for
      #   --certificatesresolvers.dns.acme.httpchallenge=true
      #   --certificatesresolvers.dns.acme.httpchallenge.entrypoint=web
      # The two values are not ${VAR:?...}: compose interpolates before it
      # applies profiles, so the demand would hit the external-Traefik mode
      # too. Missing, they land in Traefik's log as an unknown provider.
      - "--certificatesresolvers.dns.acme.dnschallenge=true"
      - "--certificatesresolvers.dns.acme.dnschallenge.provider=${RADM_DNS_PROVIDER:-MISSING-set-RADM_DNS_PROVIDER-in-deploy/.env}"
      - "--certificatesresolvers.dns.acme.email=${RADM_ACME_EMAIL:-MISSING-set-RADM_ACME_EMAIL-in-deploy/.env}"
      - "--certificatesresolvers.dns.acme.storage=/letsencrypt/acme.json"
      # Do NOT add forwardedheaders.insecure or .trustedips: by default Traefik
      # replaces the client's X-Forwarded-*, and that header is the IP in the
      # audit log and the key the login rate limit counts against.
    env_file:
      # Traefik's alone, so that RADM_SECRET_KEY never reaches the process
      # holding the Docker socket. Only DNS-01 needs it, hence optional.
      - path: .env.dns
        required: false
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      # The socket is root on the host, :ro or not — the API can start a
      # privileged container. If that is too much trust for a proxy, put
      # tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy in front of it with CONTAINERS=1.
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - traefik-acme:/letsencrypt
    networks: [proxy]

volumes:
  radm-data:
  traefik-acme:

networks:
  # Ours with the bundled Traefik; your proxy's existing one when
  # RADM_TRAEFIK_NETWORK_EXTERNAL=true.
  proxy:
    name: ${RADM_TRAEFIK_NETWORK:-radm}
    external: ${RADM_TRAEFIK_NETWORK_EXTERNAL:-false}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RADM agent installer.
#
#   curl -fsSL https://panel.example.com/install.sh | sudo bash -s -- --token <TOKEN>
#
# Enrolls this device with the panel, installs the agent as a systemd service,
# and authorises the panel's SSH key for the login user so the web terminal and
# file browser work immediately.
set -euo pipefail

PANEL_URL="__PANEL_URL__"   # substituted by the panel when it serves this file
TOKEN=""
SSH_USER=""
ALLOW="loopback"
INSECURE=0
FORCE=0

BIN=/usr/local/bin/radm-agent.pyz
CONFIG_DIR=/etc/radm
STATE_DIR=/var/lib/radm
UNIT=/etc/systemd/system/radm-agent.service

die()  { printf '\033[31merror:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
info() { printf '\033[36m::\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[32m ✓\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --token)    TOKEN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --url)      PANEL_URL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --allow)    ALLOW="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --insecure) INSECURE=1; shift ;;
        --force)    FORCE=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help)
            sed -n '2,10p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
done

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || die "run this with sudo"

# An enrollment token is only needed the first time; re-running to upgrade the
# agent reuses the registration already on disk.
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ] && { [ ! -f "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" ] || [ "$FORCE" -eq 1 ]; }; then
    die "missing --token (create one in the panel under Enroll)"
fi

# Validate by shape rather than by comparing against the placeholder: the panel
# rewrites every occurrence of it when serving this file, so a literal
# comparison here would end up comparing the URL against itself.
case "$PANEL_URL" in
    http://*|https://*) ;;
    *) die "missing --url (panel address)" ;;
esac

command -v curl >/dev/null || die "curl is required"
PYTHON=$(command -v python3) || die "python3 is required (Debian: apt install python3)"

PY_OK=$("$PYTHON" -c 'import sys; print(1 if sys.version_info >= (3,9) else 0)')
[ "$PY_OK" = "1" ] || die "python 3.9 or newer is required; found $("$PYTHON" -V)"

CURL_OPTS=(-fsSL)
[ "$INSECURE" -eq 1 ] && CURL_OPTS+=(-k)

# Re-running the installer must not create a second device record for the same
# board: upgrading the agent is a normal thing to do, and silently duplicating
# the device would leave a permanently offline ghost in the panel.
EXISTING_TOKEN=""
if [ -f "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" ] && [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ]; then
    EXISTING_TOKEN=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*token[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" | head -1)
fi

if [ -n "$EXISTING_TOKEN" ]; then
    info "already enrolled — upgrading the agent, keeping the existing registration"
    info "(pass --force to register this board as a new device instead)"
    DEVICE_TOKEN="[REDACTED]"
    WS_URL=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*url[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" | head -1)
    SSH_KEY=""
    EXISTING_USER=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*ssh_user[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" | head -1)
    [ -n "$EXISTING_USER" ] && SSH_USER="$EXISTING_USER"
    ok "reusing the existing registration"
else

info "enrolling with $PANEL_URL"

HOSTNAME_VALUE=$(hostname)
ARCH=$(uname -m)
OS_RELEASE=$(. /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null && echo "${PRETTY_NAME:-}" || echo "")
MODEL=$( (tr -d '\0' < /proc/device-tree/model) 2>/dev/null || echo "")

PAYLOAD=$("$PYTHON" - "$TOKEN" "$HOSTNAME_VALUE" "$ARCH" "$OS_RELEASE" "$MODEL" <<'PY'
import json, sys
keys = ("token", "hostname", "arch", "os_release", "model")
print(json.dumps(dict(zip(keys, sys.argv[1:6]))))
PY
)

RESPONSE=$(curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" -X POST "$PANEL_URL/api/enroll" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$PAYLOAD") \
    || die "enrollment failed — check the token and that the panel is reachable"

# The login user comes from the enrollment token, i.e. from whoever created it
# in the panel — not from this script. A board must not get to nominate the
# account the panel logs into, or it could ask for root and this script would
# dutifully authorise the panel's key there.
read -r DEVICE_TOKEN WS_URL SSH_USER SSH_KEY <<EOF
$("$PYTHON" - "$RESPONSE" <<'PY'
import json, sys
data = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
print(data["device_token"], data["ws_url"], data["ssh_user"],
      data["ssh_public_key"].replace(" ", "\x1f"))
PY
)
EOF
SSH_KEY=$(printf '%s' "$SSH_KEY" | tr '\037' ' ')
[ -n "$DEVICE_TOKEN" ] || die "panel did not return a device token"
getent passwd "$SSH_USER" >/dev/null \
    || die "the panel expects to log in as '$SSH_USER', but there is no such user here.
       Create it, or change the SSH user in the panel under Device → Settings."
ok "enrolled; the panel will log in as '$SSH_USER'"

fi  # end of "already enrolled" branch

info "installing agent"
curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" -o "$BIN.tmp" "$PANEL_URL/agent/radm-agent.pyz" \
    || die "could not download the agent"
chmod 0755 "$BIN.tmp"
mv "$BIN.tmp" "$BIN"
ok "installed $BIN"

install -d -m 0750 "$CONFIG_DIR"
install -d -m 0755 "$STATE_DIR"

umask 077
cat > "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" <<EOF
# Written by install.sh on $(date -Is)
url = $WS_URL
token = [REDACTED]
state_dir = $STATE_DIR
allow = $ALLOW
# Recorded for uninstall.sh: it needs to know whose key to take out.
ssh_user = $SSH_USER
verify_tls = $([ "$INSECURE" -eq 1 ] && echo false || echo true)
EOF
chmod 0600 "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf"
ok "wrote $CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf"

# Authorise the panel's key so the terminal and file browser work. This is
# what lets the panel use real SSH instead of the agent handing out a shell.
if [ -n "$SSH_KEY" ]; then
    HOME_DIR=$(getent passwd "$SSH_USER" | cut -d: -f6)
    AUTH="$HOME_DIR/.ssh/authorized_keys"
    install -d -m 0700 -o "$SSH_USER" -g "$(id -gn "$SSH_USER")" "$HOME_DIR/.ssh"
    touch "$AUTH"
    if ! grep -qF "$SSH_KEY" "$AUTH" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '%s\n' "$SSH_KEY" >> "$AUTH"
    fi
    chmod 0600 "$AUTH"
    chown "$SSH_USER":"$(id -gn "$SSH_USER")" "$AUTH"
    ok "authorised the panel key for $SSH_USER"
fi

if command -v systemctl >/dev/null && [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
    curl "${CURL_OPTS[@]}" -o "$UNIT" "$PANEL_URL/agent/radm-agent.service" \
        || die "could not download the systemd unit"
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl enable --now radm-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl restart radm-agent
    sleep 2
    if systemctl is-active --quiet radm-agent; then
        ok "radm-agent is running"
    else
        printf '\033[33m!\033[0m agent did not start; check: journalctl -u radm-agent -n 50\n'
    fi
else
    printf '\033[33m!\033[0m no systemd here; start the agent yourself:\n    %s --config %s\n' \
        "$BIN" "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf"
fi

# Check for a live sshd directly: systemctl is not available everywhere this
# runs (containers, minimal images), and its absence is not evidence.
if ! pgrep -x sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '\033[33m!\033[0m sshd does not appear to be running — the web terminal and file browser need it\n'
fi

printf '\n\033[32mDone.\033[0m This device should now appear in the panel.\n'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove the RADM agent from a device.
#
#   curl -fsSL https://panel.example.com/uninstall.sh | sudo bash
#
# Stops and removes the service, the binary, the config and the state. The
# panel's key comes out of authorized_keys too — otherwise the panel would keep
# SSH access to the board after the agent is gone.
#
# The device record in the panel is left alone: this runs on the board itself
# and has no rights to change anything on the server. Delete it in the web UI
# (Device → Settings → Delete) to erase the metrics, tunnels and key.
set -euo pipefail

KEEP_KEY=0
ASSUME_YES=0

BIN=/usr/local/bin/radm-agent.pyz
CONFIG_DIR=/etc/radm
STATE_DIR=/var/lib/radm
UNIT=/etc/systemd/system/radm-agent.service

die()  { printf '\033[31merror:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
info() { printf '\033[36m::\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[32m ✓\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[33m !\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --keep-key) KEEP_KEY=1; shift ;;
        -y|--yes)   ASSUME_YES=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help)  sed -n '2,14p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) die "unknown option: $1" ;;
    esac
done

[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] || die "run this with sudo"

if [ "$ASSUME_YES" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf 'Remove the RADM agent from this device? [y/N] '
    read -r answer </dev/tty || answer=""
    case "$answer" in
        [yY]|[yY][eE][sS]) ;;
        *) info "cancelled"; exit 0 ;;
    esac
fi

# Read the user the key was issued to out of the config, before deleting it.
SSH_USER=""
if [ -f "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" ]; then
    SSH_USER=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*ssh_user[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' "$CONFIG_DIR/agent.conf" | head -1)
fi

if command -v systemctl >/dev/null && [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then
    if systemctl list-unit-files radm-agent.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        systemctl disable --now radm-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        ok "service stopped and disabled"
    fi
    if [ -f "$UNIT" ]; then
        rm -f "$UNIT"
        systemctl daemon-reload
        systemctl reset-failed radm-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        ok "systemd unit removed"
    fi
else
    # Without systemd the agent may have been started by hand.
    if pkill -f 'radm-agent\.pyz' 2>/dev/null; then
        ok "agent process stopped"
    fi
fi

# The panel key is found by the comment install.sh puts on it: "radm@<slug>".
if [ "$KEEP_KEY" -eq 0 ]; then
    removed=0
    for home in /root /home/*; do
        auth="$home/.ssh/authorized_keys"
        [ -f "$auth" ] || continue
        if grep -q ' radm@' "$auth" 2>/dev/null; then
            tmp=$(mktemp)
            grep -v ' radm@' "$auth" > "$tmp" || true
            cat "$tmp" > "$auth"
            rm -f "$tmp"
            removed=1
            ok "panel key removed from $auth"
        fi
    done
    [ "$removed" -eq 1 ] || warn "no panel key found in authorized_keys — it may have been added by hand"
    [ -n "$SSH_USER" ] && info "the key was issued to user '$SSH_USER'"
else
    warn "panel key kept (--keep-key) — the panel retains SSH access to this device"
fi

for path in "$BIN" "$CONFIG_DIR" "$STATE_DIR"; do
    if [ -e "$path" ]; then
        rm -rf "$path"
        ok "removed: $path"
    fi
done

printf '\n\033[32mDone.\033[0m The agent has been removed.\n'
printf 'Remember to delete the device in the panel, or it will sit in the list as "offline".\n'

"""Admin login, first-run setup and password management."""

from __future__ import annotations

import secrets
import time

import pyotp
from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Request, Response, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from sqlalchemy import func, select

from radm.audit import client_ip, record
from radm.api.deps import CurrentAdmin, DbSession, load_admin
from radm.config import settings
from radm.db.models import AdminUser
from radm.security import bootstrap
from radm.security.crypto import hash_password, verify_password
from radm.security.sessions import (
    COOKIE_NAME,
    CSRF_COOKIE,
    SESSION_MAX_AGE,
    issue_session,
    login_limiter,
)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/auth", tags=["auth"])

# Burned on the unknown-user path so a login attempt costs the same either way.
# Computed once at import: bcrypt's cost is the point, but paying it twice per
# request is not.
DUMMY_HASH = hash_password(secrets.token_urlsafe(16))


class LoginRequest(BaseModel):
    username: str
    password: str
    totp: str | None = None


class SetupRequest(BaseModel):
    username: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=64)
    password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=256)
    setup_token: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)


class PasswordChange(BaseModel):
    current_password: str
    new_password: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=256)


class TotpEnable(BaseModel):
    secret: str
    code: str
    password: str


class TotpDisable(BaseModel):
    password: str


async def _admin_count(db) -> int:
    return (await db.execute(select(func.count(AdminUser.id)))).scalar_one()


def _verify_totp(secret: str, code: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Return the time step a code belongs to, or None if it does not match.

    pyotp only answers yes/no, but the caller needs to know *which* step was
    accepted so the same code cannot be presented twice.
    """
    if not code:
        return None
    totp = pyotp.TOTP(secret)
    now = int(time.time())
    for offset in (0, -1, 1):  # the same one-step tolerance verify() allows
        step = now // totp.interval + offset
        if totp.verify(code, for_time=step * totp.interval):
            return step
    return None


def _set_session_cookies(response: Response, user: AdminUser, secure: bool) -> None:
    response.set_cookie(
        COOKIE_NAME,
        issue_session(user.id, user.session_epoch),
        max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE,
        httponly=True,
        samesite="strict",
        secure=secure,
        path="/",
    )
    # Readable by JavaScript on purpose: the SPA echoes it back in a header,
    # which is what proves the request came from our own page.
    response.set_cookie(
        CSRF_COOKIE,
        secrets.token_urlsafe(24),
        max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE,
        httponly=False,
        samesite="strict",
        secure=secure,
        path="/",
    )


def _is_secure(request: Request) -> bool:
    return request.url.scheme == "https" or request.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto") == "https"


@router.get("/status")
async def auth_status(request: Request, response: Response, db: DbSession) -> dict:
    """Tells the SPA whether to show login or the first-run setup form.

    Also seeds the CSRF cookie. Login and setup are state-changing and are held
    to the same double-submit check as everything else, which needs a token to
    exist before anyone is signed in; the SPA calls this first either way.
    """
    if CSRF_COOKIE not in request.cookies:
        response.set_cookie(
            CSRF_COOKIE,
            secrets.token_urlsafe(24),
            max_age=SESSION_MAX_AGE,
            httponly=False,
            samesite="strict",
            secure=_is_secure(request),
            path="/",
        )
    return {"configured": await _admin_count(db) > 0}


@router.post("/setup")
async def setup(payload: SetupRequest, request: Request, response: Response, db: DbSession) -> dict:
    ip = client_ip(request) or "unknown"
    if not login_limiter.check(ip):
        raise HTTPException(
            status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, "too many attempts; try again later"
        )

    if await _admin_count(db) > 0:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT, "already configured")

    # Creating the first administrator hands over the whole fleet, so it takes
    # the token the panel printed at startup — not merely the absence of a user.
    if not bootstrap.verify(payload.setup_token):
        await record(db, "admin.setup_rejected", actor=payload.username, request=request)
        await db.commit()
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, "invalid setup token")

    user = AdminUser(
        username=payload.username,
        password_hash=hash_password(payload.password),
    )
    db.add(user)
    await db.flush()
    await record(db, "admin.setup", actor=user.username, request=request)
    await db.commit()

    bootstrap.clear(settings.data_dir)
    login_limiter.reset(ip)
    _set_session_cookies(response, user, _is_secure(request))
    return {"ok": True, "username": user.username}


@router.post("/login")
async def login(payload: LoginRequest, request: Request, response: Response, db: DbSession) -> dict:
    ip = client_ip(request) or "unknown"
    if not login_limiter.check(ip):
        raise HTTPException(
            status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, "too many attempts; try again later"
        )

    user = (
        await db.execute(select(AdminUser).where(AdminUser.username == payload.username))
    ).scalars().first()

    # Same response for unknown user and wrong password, so the endpoint does
    # not confirm which usernames exist. The hash has to be checked either way:
    # skipping bcrypt when there is no such user returns in a fraction of the
    # time, and that difference is a perfectly good username oracle.
    if user is None or not verify_password(payload.password, user.password_hash):
        if user is None:
            verify_password(payload.password, DUMMY_HASH)
        await record(
            db, "auth.login_failed", actor=payload.username, request=request
        )
        await db.commit()
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "invalid credentials")

    if user.totp_secret:
        step = _verify_totp(user.totp_secret, payload.totp)
        if step is None or step <= user.totp_last_step:
            # A code already used is refused for the rest of its window: it is
            # valid for 30 seconds either way, which is plenty of time for one
            # shoulder-surfed or phished from a proxy to be replayed.
            await record(db, "auth.totp_failed", actor=user.username, request=request)
            await db.commit()
            raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "invalid two-factor code")
        user.totp_last_step = step

    login_limiter.reset(ip)
    _set_session_cookies(response, user, _is_secure(request))
    await record(db, "auth.login", actor=user.username, request=request)
    await db.commit()

    return {"ok": True, "username": user.username, "totp_enabled": bool(user.totp_secret)}


@router.post("/logout")
async def logout(request: Request, response: Response, db: DbSession) -> dict:
    """Sign out, retiring the cookie server-side as well as in the browser.

    Clearing the cookie only affects the browser doing the clearing. The token
    itself stays valid for its full 14 days, so anyone who captured it — a
    shared machine, a proxy log — would still hold a working session. Bumping
    the epoch is what actually ends it.
    """
    user = await load_admin(db, request.cookies.get(COOKIE_NAME))
    if user is not None:
        user.session_epoch += 1
        await record(db, "auth.logout", actor=user.username, request=request)
        await db.commit()

    response.delete_cookie(COOKIE_NAME, path="/")
    response.delete_cookie(CSRF_COOKIE, path="/")
    return {"ok": True}


@router.get("/me")
async def me(user: CurrentAdmin) -> dict:
    return {"username": user.username, "totp_enabled": bool(user.totp_secret)}


@router.post("/password")
async def change_password(
    payload: PasswordChange, user: CurrentAdmin, request: Request, response: Response, db: DbSession
) -> dict:
    if not verify_password(payload.current_password, user.password_hash):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "current password is incorrect")

    user.password_hash = hash_password(payload.new_password)
    user.session_epoch += 1  # invalidate every existing session
    await record(db, "admin.password_changed", actor=user.username, request=request)
    await db.commit()

    _set_session_cookies(response, user, _is_secure(request))
    return {"ok": True}


@router.post("/totp/init")
async def totp_init(user: CurrentAdmin) -> dict:
    """Generate a candidate secret; it is only stored once a code confirms it."""
    secret = [REDACTED]
    uri = pyotp.TOTP(secret).provisioning_uri(name=user.username, issuer_name="RADM")
    return {"secret": secret, "uri": uri}


@router.post("/totp/enable")
async def totp_enable(
    payload: TotpEnable, user: CurrentAdmin, request: Request, db: DbSession
) -> dict:
    # Changing the second factor takes the first one. Otherwise a borrowed
    # session — the whole thing 2FA is meant to survive — could rebind the
    # account to an authenticator the attacker holds.
    if not verify_password(payload.password, user.password_hash):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "password is incorrect")

    step = _verify_totp(payload.secret, payload.code)
    if step is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, "code does not match")

    user.totp_secret = [REDACTED]
    user.totp_last_step = step
    await record(db, "admin.totp_enabled", actor=user.username, request=request)
    await db.commit()
    return {"ok": True}


@router.post("/totp/disable")
async def totp_disable(
    payload: TotpDisable, user: CurrentAdmin, request: Request, db: DbSession
) -> dict:
    if not verify_password(payload.password, user.password_hash):
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, "password is incorrect")

    user.totp_secret = None
    user.totp_last_step = 0
    await record(db, "admin.totp_disabled", actor=user.username, request=request)
    await db.commit()
    return {"ok": True}

def test_referer_places_a_subresource_in_its_own_tunnel():
    """Two shared links open in one browser must not fight over the routing.

    A device page pulls "/static/app.js" against the origin root, so the tunnel
    prefix is gone from the request. The Referer still has it, and reading it
    per request — rather than remembering one tunnel per browser — is what lets

def test_agent_refuses_an_update_from_another_host():
    """The digest ships with the URL, so it is the origin that bounds this.

    The update ends in os.execv on the downloaded file, as root.

        "http://panel.example.com/agent.pyz",

Every board this code targets formats its load differently, and almost none of
them are available on the machine running the tests — a Rockchip NPU, a Jetson
iGPU and an AMD card cannot all be present at once. Writing the exact bytes
those kernels produce into a temp directory is the only way to keep the parsers
honest, so the formats are pinned here rather than discovered in production.

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "agent"))

from radm_agent import accel  # noqa: E402


@pytest.fixture
def sysfs(tmp_path):
    def write(relative: str, content: str) -> str:
        path = tmp_path / relative
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(content)
        return str(path)

    return write

def test_rknpu_three_cores(sysfs):
    """RK3588 debugfs output, verbatim down to the spacing."""
    path = sysfs("load", "NPU load:  Core0: 60%, Core1:  0%, Core2: 30%,\n")
    probe = accel._Rknpu("rknpu", "Rockchip NPU (3 cores)", path)

    sample = probe.sample()
    assert sample["load_pct"] == pytest.approx(30.0)  # mean, like cpu_pct
    assert sample["cores"] == [60.0, 0.0, 30.0]
    assert sample["kind"] == "npu"


def test_rknpu_single_core(sysfs):
    """RK3568 prints one figure and no per-core breakdown."""
    path = sysfs("load", "NPU load:  42%\n")
    sample = accel._Rknpu("rknpu", "Rockchip NPU (1 core)", path).sample()

    assert sample["load_pct"] == pytest.approx(42.0)
    assert "cores" not in sample

    """debugfs unmounted, or the driver replaced: absent, not idle."""
    probe = accel._Rknpu("rknpu", "Rockchip NPU", str(Path(sysfs("x", "")).parent / "gone"))
    assert probe.sample()["load_pct"] is None

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build radm-agent.pyz: a single self-contained file with websockets vendored in.
#
# A zipapp means deployment is "copy one file" — no venv, no pip, no compiler on
# the device. `websockets` is pure Python, so the result runs on any CPU
# architecture without a rebuild, which is the whole point when the fleet mixes
# armv6, armv7 and aarch64.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(dirname "$HERE")"
BUILD="$HERE/build"
DIST="$HERE/dist"
PYTHON="${PYTHON:-python3}"

rm -rf "$BUILD"
mkdir -p "$BUILD" "$DIST"

# -L dereferences: radm_agent/mux.py is a symlink to the canonical shared copy
# in shared/radm_mux.py, and the archive must hold the real file.
cp -rL "$HERE/radm_agent" "$BUILD/radm_agent"

# --python-version resolves against the oldest Python the installer accepts
# (install/install.sh: 3.9+), not against the interpreter doing the build. Without it
# pip picks the newest websockets — 17.x needs 3.11 and dies on a device with
# 3.10 at "cannot import name 'Self' from typing", long after the installer has
# already reported success. The floor is 14 because that is where
# websockets.connect became the new asyncio client with additional_headers.
# --only-binary is what makes --python-version legal for pip.

"""Agent configuration: a small INI-less key=value file plus CLI overrides."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import sys
from typing import Dict, Optional

if sys.platform == "win32":
    # %ProgramData% is the Windows answer to /etc plus /var/lib: machine-wide,
    # writable by services, and outside any user profile. The installer creates
    # both paths and restricts their ACLs, since the config holds the token.
    _PROGRAM_DATA = os.environ.get("ProgramData", r"C:\ProgramData")
    DEFAULT_CONFIG = os.path.join(_PROGRAM_DATA, "RADM", "agent.conf")
    DEFAULT_STATE = os.path.join(_PROGRAM_DATA, "RADM", "state")
else:
    DEFAULT_CONFIG = "/etc/radm/agent.conf"
    DEFAULT_STATE = "/var/lib/radm"


class Config:
    def __init__(self, values: Dict[str, str]) -> None:
        self.url = values.get("url", "")
        self.token = values.get("token", "")
        self.state_dir = values.get("state_dir", DEFAULT_STATE)
        self.metrics_interval = int(values.get("metrics_interval", "10") or 10)
        self.verify_tls = values.get("verify_tls", "true").lower() != "false"

        # Targets the panel is allowed to ask us to dial. Restricting this by
        # default means a compromised panel cannot turn the fleet into an open
        # proxy into each device's LAN.
        raw_allow = values.get("allow", "loopback")
        self.allow = [item.strip() for item in raw_allow.split(",") if item.strip()]

    def validate(self) -> None:
        if not self.url:
            raise SystemExit("radm-agent: no panel URL configured")
        if not self.token:
            raise SystemExit("radm-agent: no device token configured")

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Config(url={self.url!r}, state_dir={self.state_dir!r}, allow={self.allow})"


def read_file(path: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    values: Dict[str, str] = {}
    try:
        with open(path, "r") as handle:
            for line in handle:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                key, _, value = line.partition("=")
                values[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    except OSError:
        pass
    return values


def load(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> Config:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="radm-agent", description="RADM device agent")
    parser.add_argument("--config", default=os.environ.get("RADM_AGENT_CONFIG", DEFAULT_CONFIG))
    parser.add_argument("--url", help="panel websocket URL, e.g. wss://panel.example.com/api/agent/ws")
    parser.add_argument("--token", help="device token")
    parser.add_argument("--state-dir", help="where to buffer metrics while offline")
    parser.add_argument("--interval", type=int, help="seconds between metric snapshots")
    parser.add_argument("--allow", help="comma-separated dial targets: loopback, private, any")
    parser.add_argument("--insecure", action="store_true", help="skip TLS verification")
    parser.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="print one metrics snapshot and exit")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", "-v", action="store_true")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    values = read_file(args.config)

    # Environment sits between the file and explicit flags.
    for key, env in (
        ("url", "RADM_URL"),
        ("token", "RADM_TOKEN"),
        ("state_dir", "RADM_STATE_DIR"),
        ("allow", "RADM_ALLOW"),
    ):
        if os.environ.get(env):
            values[key] = os.environ[env]

    if args.url:
        values["url"] = args.url
    if args.token:
        values["token"] = args.token
    if args.state_dir:
        values["state_dir"] = args.state_dir
    if args.interval:
        values["metrics_interval"] = str(args.interval)
    if args.allow:
        values["allow"] = args.allow
    if args.insecure:
        values["verify_tls"] = "false"

    config = Config(values)
    config.cli = args  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    return config

"""Metric collection.

No psutil: it is a C extension, and requiring a compiler or a matching wheel on
every armv6/armv7/aarch64 board is exactly the kind of friction that makes an
agent hard to deploy. Everything here is stdlib and Python 3.9 compatible.

The platform-specific readings live in ``collect_linux`` and ``collect_windows``
and return *cumulative counters*. Turning those into rates needs the previous
sample, so that state and the arithmetic around it stay here — one
implementation, identical behaviour on both platforms, and the panel never has
to reason about counter resets across reboots.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import time
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from radm_agent import accel

if sys.platform == "win32":
    from radm_agent import collect_windows as source
else:
    from radm_agent import collect_linux as source


class Collector:
    """Stateful collector: rates need the previous sample."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._prev_cpu: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None
        self._prev_cores: Dict[str, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
        self._prev_net: Optional[Tuple[float, int, int]] = None
        # Which GPUs and NPUs this board has cannot change while the agent
        # runs, so the search for them happens exactly once.
        self._accels = accel.detect()

    # --- cpu -----------------------------------------------------------

    def _cpu(self) -> Tuple[float, List[float]]:
        total_times, core_times = source.read_cpu()

        overall = 0.0
        if total_times is not None:
            busy, total = total_times
            if self._prev_cpu is not None:
                prev_busy, prev_total = self._prev_cpu
                delta_total = total - prev_total
                if delta_total > 0:
                    overall = round(100.0 * (busy - prev_busy) / delta_total, 1)
            self._prev_cpu = total_times

        cores: List[float] = []
        for name, (busy, total) in core_times:
            prev = self._prev_cores.get(name)
            if prev is not None:
                delta_total = total - prev[1]
                if delta_total > 0:
                    cores.append(round(100.0 * (busy - prev[0]) / delta_total, 1))
                else:
                    cores.append(0.0)
            self._prev_cores[name] = (busy, total)

        return max(0.0, min(overall, 100.0)), cores

    # --- network ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _network(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        totals = source.read_network()
        if totals is None:
            return {"net_rx": 0.0, "net_tx": 0.0}

        rx_total, tx_total = totals
        now = time.time()
        rates = {"net_rx": 0.0, "net_tx": 0.0}

        if self._prev_net is not None:
            prev_time, prev_rx, prev_tx = self._prev_net
            elapsed = now - prev_time
            # Negative deltas mean an interface disappeared or counters wrapped;
            # report zero rather than a nonsense spike.
            if elapsed > 0 and rx_total >= prev_rx and tx_total >= prev_tx:
                rates = {
                    "net_rx": round((rx_total - prev_rx) / elapsed, 1),
                    "net_tx": round((tx_total - prev_tx) / elapsed, 1),
                }

        self._prev_net = (now, rx_total, tx_total)
        return rates

    # --- assembly ---------------------------------------------------------

    def snapshot(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        cpu_pct, cpu_cores = self._cpu()
        data: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "t": "metrics",
            "ts": int(time.time()),
            "cpu_pct": cpu_pct,
            "cpu_cores": cpu_cores,
            "disks": source.read_disks(),
            "temp_c": source.read_temperature(),
            "uptime_s": source.read_uptime(),
            "throttled": source.read_throttled(),
        }
        accels = accel.sample(self._accels)
        if accels:
            data["accels"] = accels
        data.update(source.read_memory())
        data.update(source.read_load())
        data.update(self._network())
        return data


def system_info() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Facts sent once in `hello`."""
    facts = source.system_facts()
    facts["accelerators"] = accel.inventory(accel.detect())
    return facts
